title: Value Stream Mapping and Management
group: Value streams, AI and other frameworks (10%)

header.html: Value stream identification, mapping and management (5%)

Define value stream, core value stream, enabling value stream, value stream mapping, value stream management and complexity thinking; understand the difference between core and enabling streams; understand how workflows are optimized for complexity; know the purpose of mapping and management, their relationship, and the elements of a value stream map
the official ITIL Foundation (Version 5) syllabus, version 5.0 (February 2026), category 5

toc.title: Elements of a value stream map

html:
1Value streams

A value stream is the series of steps an organization takes to create and deliver products and services to consumers: from demand to value.

Type Meaning Example
Core value stream Delivers value directly to a consumer Handling a customer order from request to delivery
Enabling value stream Supports the core streams inside the organization Hiring, finance, supplier management, tooling
Exam tip

. Core = the consumer feels it. Enabling = it helps the core streams work.

2Value stream mapping and management

Term Meaning
Value stream mapping (VSM) Drawing the steps, flows and waits of a value stream to see how work really moves
Value stream management (VSM) Continuously managing and improving value streams using what the map shows

Purpose: to find waste, delay and handoffs, agree where to improve, and improve flow and value. Relationship: mapping shows, management improves. The map is the tool; management is the ongoing discipline that uses it. [Verify live]

3Elements of a value stream map

Element What it shows
Steps / activities The work done at each stage
Flow and handoffs Where work moves from one team or tool to another
Time Process time (working) and wait time (queueing)
Roles and tools Who and what is involved
Information flow How demand and data travel
Waste and problems Delays, rework, defects to fix

[Verify live] Exact element names may differ in the official book; the idea is to visualize steps, flow and time.

4Complexity thinking

Complexity thinking recognizes that many situations are complex: cause and effect cannot be fully predicted, parts interact, and change creates surprises. Workflows are therefore optimized for complexity with short cycles, experiments, feedback, autonomy for teams and learning, instead of rigid, fully planned processes. It links to progress iteratively with feedback and VUCA (Module 3).

Exam tip

. Complex = unpredictable, so probe, learn and adapt. Complicated = knowable with expertise. ITIL pushes iteration and feedback when work is complex.

Exam tip

. Mapping draws the stream; management improves it. If a question asks who benefits directly, core streams reach consumers and enabling streams support them.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which value stream delivers value directly to consumers?

  • ACore value stream
  • BEnabling value stream
  • CGovernance stream
  • DSupport stream only
Show the answer

Answer: A. A core value stream delivers value directly.

S2A mapping workshop shows an order waits five days between two teams. What is the likely next step?

  • AIgnore it, because wait time is not important
  • BImprove the handoff, using value stream management
  • CDelete the value stream map
  • DDeclare the order a known error
Show the answer

Answer: B. The map reveals delay, and management improves it.

S3Which statements about value stream mapping and management are CORRECT? (1) Mapping visualizes how work moves. (2) Management continuously improves value streams. (3) Mapping is an ongoing management discipline that replaces management. (4) A map shows only the final result and ignores wait time.

  • A1 and 2
  • B3 and 4
  • C2 and 3
  • D1 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: A. Mapping visualizes, management improves.

S4Identify the missing word(s). A(n) [ ? ] value stream supports the core value streams inside the organization.

  • AConsumer
  • BEnabling
  • CComplex
  • DDisaster
Show the answer

Answer: B. Enabling value streams support the core ones.

S5Work is unpredictable and parts interact in surprising ways. Which approach does complexity thinking favor?

  • APlan everything in detail first and never change the plan
  • BRemove all teams' autonomy
  • CIgnore feedback until the end
  • DShort cycles, experiments and feedback
Show the answer

Answer: D. Complex work calls for iteration and learning.

S6Hiring and finance processes keep the organization running but are not seen by consumers. Which type of stream are they?

  • ACore
  • BConsumer-facing
  • CGovernance-only
  • DEnabling
Show the answer

Answer: D. They support the core streams.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Define a value stream.

Show the answer

The series of steps an organization takes to create and deliver products and services.

R2What is the difference between core and enabling value streams?

Show the answer

Core delivers value directly to consumers; enabling supports the core streams.

R3What does value stream mapping do?

Show the answer

Visualizes the steps, flow and waits of a value stream.

R4What does value stream management do?

Show the answer

Continuously manages and improves value streams.

R5What is complexity thinking?

Show the answer

Recognizing that cause and effect are not fully predictable and working with iteration and feedback.

R6Name two things a value stream map shows.

Show the answer

Steps and handoffs, and process and wait time.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Value stream steps from demand to value
Core / enabling consumer feels it / supports the core
Mapping / management shows the flow / improves it
Map elements steps, flow, time, roles, information, waste
Complexity thinking unpredictable; iterate with feedback
